summary: Observations a few days apart by two motorists of a bright light and malfunctioning vehicles: lack of reliable information.
description: GEIPAN conducts re-examinations of old cases in order to be more relevant in its conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the past few years, this re-examination sometimes leads to a change in classification. The present re-examination concerns two observation cases previously classified as D and named BROYES (51) 10.01.2000 and SOMMESOUS (51) 31.12.1999. On January 10, 2000, between 9:00 PM and 9:05 PM, a motorist on the D39 near the Broyes (51) water tower was suddenly blinded by a very intense light that entered the car through the sunroof. The engine and the car radio stopped abruptly, but the ignition remained on. According to the witness, after a minute, the phenomenon dissipated, the car radio started working again, and he was able to restart his car and drive home, terrified. Following a phone call from the Gendarmerie's Operations Center, officers immediately went to the home of the deeply shaken witness and then to the location of the sighting. They observed that the sky was clear and full of stars (shooting stars) and that air traffic was significant and visible (flashing lights). The temperature was wintry but without frost. No disruption to the power lines along the road was observed. Furthermore, there was no street lighting in that area. According to military sources, no flights were reported that evening. The on-site investigation by SEPRA and the reconstruction in the vehicle determined that the sighting lasted between 15 and 30 seconds maximum, instead of the one minute initially reported by the witness. During the investigation, the gendarmerie found another witness who had observed a similar phenomenon a few days earlier. On December 31, 1999, between 7:30 and 8:00 PM, a motorist driving on the N4 near Sommesous (51) was blinded by a white flash. No sound was heard. All the dashboard lights came on, and the car's engine suddenly stopped, putting the car in neutral. The engine quickly restarted on its own. A check by a mechanic, initiated by the witness, of the battery terminals revealed nothing abnormal. We have two cases of observation with close spatial (a few kilometers) and temporal (10 days) proximity, presenting a strong apparent similarity (see the single investigation report for both cases): - an unlocalized light (or flash) perceived by the driver of a car; - Engine stopped, dashboard malfunctions. The case of BROYES (51) 10.01.2000 is even stranger insofar as the light was blinding and entered the vehicle. No physical explanation can be considered, the description is so bizarre. We can only formulate the hypothesis of strangeness induced or accentuated by the witness himself, but we have no evidence to support this: - the witness watched the X-Files series on television shortly before the events, when M6 was broadcasting season 4, which contains a scene where a UFO flies over a vehicle and illuminates it with a dazzling white light. The witness may have experienced a genuine strangeness that evening and been influenced, consciously or unconsciously, by science fiction when remembering or recounting the events; - The young witness, living with his parents, may have been traumatized by an event unrelated to the UFO and unable, for a reason related to his occasional drug use (self-reported) or for some other reason, to explain his condition to his parents upon returning home other than by inventing an experience directly inspired by The X-Files. In the case of SOMMESOUS (51) on December 31, 1999, the physical hypotheses (meteor, camera flash, or firework burst a few hours before the turn of the millennium) lack any supporting evidence. The consistency of these observation cases is POOR. Case of Broyes (51) 10/01/2000: - In terms of information, although an investigation was conducted on site by the gendarmerie and SEPRA (GEIPAN at the time) shortly after the events, we only have a brief report of this investigation. No audio, video, or written recordings of the various interviews and reconstructions that took place during this investigation are included in the file; - In terms of reliability, one can question the possible influence of science fiction given the similarity of the account to a scene from the X-Files series (see above). One can also question the influence of occasional drug use (see above). In the case of SOMMESOUS (51) on December 31, 1999: - in terms of information: the gendarmerie conducted no investigation beyond the witness's interview because SEPRA did not request or investigate anything, and the gendarmerie did not perceive sufficient interest from SEPRA to conduct its own investigation; - in terms of reliability: the statement was not spontaneous. The witness, who had heard the account of the BROYES (51) case prior to his interview, may naturally have been impressed by this account and drawn parallels with his own experience, thereby increasing its strangeness and unwittingly influencing certain aspects of his statement. Only a genuine on-site investigation would have allowed: - the exploration and perhaps validation of one of the physical hypotheses (see above) specific to this case; - or, conversely, confirm a sufficiently broad range of similarities between the two cases to consider them as stemming from the same phenomenon, and based on this, by cross-referencing the information: o potentially formulate hypotheses to explain this phenomenon; o at a minimum, increase the consistency of this observation to two testimonies. The strangeness of the two cases, although unequal, is significant. The consistency is too weak to support an unexplained nature in either case or in both. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the two cases as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observations of bright white points in the night sky two years in a row: lack of information.
description: Recent report (June 5, 2014) of an old observation. On December 14, 1990, at 10:30 PM, a witness observed four white lights in a line: three of them formed a triangle while the fourth rotated around it, then the lights aligned and moved rapidly eastward. The phenomenon recurred in March 2000. The observation of lights forming and rapidly crossing the sky in a straight line suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. GEIPAN was unable to easily access the weather report for that day (too old for websites), so this hypothesis could not be verified. Lacking this information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a large, light white spiral: lack of information.
description: Recent report (June 18, 2014) of an old sighting where the witness does not remember the date. One winter evening at 1:00 AM, a witness closing their gate was startled by the presence of a large, silent, light white spiral moving by. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. This atypical sighting may suggest an exceptional meteorological event. However, the account is old, lacking in detail, and the precise date is unknown. GEIPAN cannot investigate this case due to a lack of information; it is therefore classified as "C".

summary: Observation of a ball of intense light.
description: On November 11, 1999, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness was on his roof adjusting his television antenna when he observed a very bright ball of light. The witness filmed the phenomenon for several minutes. No further information is available regarding this observation.

summary: Observation of two stationary luminous spheres
description: On October 26, 1999, at approximately 6:45 a.m., a witness observed a sphere the size of an orange attached to another sphere the size of a walnut, both stationary very far away and very high in the sky. The observation lasted 3 to 4 minutes. No further information was collected about this sighting.

summary: Observation of a very bright point of light for several days: lack of information.
description: On September 23, 24, and 25, 1999, around 6:00 AM, several witnesses from two neighboring houses observed a bright, stationary white glow that disappeared with sunrise. The observation was also made in the evening around 10:15 PM. The phenomenon was silent and so bright that it was difficult to observe with binoculars. No further information is available regarding this observation.

summary: Observation of the movement of a brown shape with sudden changes in direction
description: On the night of August 7-8, 1999, between 11:30 PM and 1:30 AM, an amateur astronomer observing the Andromeda Galaxy spotted an object moving at a constant speed along a north-south trajectory. After a few moments, the trajectory abruptly changed direction, shifting to north-northwest before returning to the north. The observed phenomenon was silent, non-luminous, and brown in color. The sketch made by the witness depicts it as barrel-shaped. The observation lasted approximately one minute. A thorough investigation with nearby airfields, as well as with civil and military authorities, failed to link the observation to an aircraft, either through examination of air traffic or radar traces. This phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On August 26, 1999, at approximately 8:10 PM, the pilot of a flight bound for Paris CDG observed a white, incandescent sphere passing by for about 5 seconds, descending more than 10 km from the aircraft. This observation was likely that of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a pendulum-like point of light
description: On August 19, 1999, at 1:00 AM, two gendarmes on patrol observed a very bright point of light in the sky with three bright blue, green, and red points rotating rapidly around it. The phenomenon occasionally exhibited a pendulum-like motion. No further information was available regarding this observation, which lasted approximately 20 minutes.

summary: Observation of a bright point dancing in the sky
description: On August 11, 1999, at approximately 4:30 a.m., an insomniac witness observed a very bright point of light with two pale green beams. This point appeared to be dancing in the sky. No further information is available.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement and along an upward trajectory of an orange glow with halo: lack of information.
description: On August 1, 1991, at 8:46 PM, a pilot off duty at home reported by telephone seeing a non-incandescent object, described as an orange glow, moving in a straight line on an ascending trajectory. This object was surrounded by a halo. No further information could be obtained.

summary: Observation of the passage of a dark triangle illuminated by three peripheral lights and a central light.
description: This old sighting from August 1999 (the witness does not specify the date and hesitates between August 1999 and August 1998) was reported in the form of a rather vague questionnaire on February 6, 2011. The testimony is unique and inconsistent, despite apparently being an observation made by a group of people. Without a precise date (the witness does not specify the date and hesitates on the year) and without any other corroborating evidence or testimonies, any investigation is impossible.

summary: Atmospheric return
description: On July 25th at 5:30 AM, two gendarmes on patrol observed from their vehicle the very rapid passage of a red and green fireball followed by a trail of smoke. Several other witnesses came forward, and the press reported on this sighting, which was very likely a meteorite or space debris re-entry.

summary: Observation of techs on slides.
description: In June 1999, a glider pilot took landscape photos and noticed unidentified teche on the slides that he hadn't seen while taking the pictures. He believed they were UFOs. This type of testimony based on photos without visual correlation is generally unusable, as the observed teche could also be lens flares or teche during the development process.

summary: Successive observations during the summer of 1999 of different movements of luminous phenomena in the night sky: lack of information.
description: Successive observations were made between June 7, 1999, and the end of August 1999. In 2008, the witness reported observations of luminous phenomena moving across the night sky. Only one testimony was collected. This testimony is not usable by GEIPAN (the French National Geographic Institute). It consists of a series of separate observations reported 10 years after the events, without specifying the precise dates of each. Consequently, the observations are numerous, disparate, and imprecise. However, they do not appear incompatible with observations of satellites, shooting stars (especially in August), or even celestial bodies. Therefore, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Multiple observations in the night sky of a luminous mass followed by a triangular-shaped cloud: very likely observations of an M45 or M4 defense missile launch in the Bay of Biscay from off the coast of Brittany.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. The observation case previously classified as D and named (DPT) HAUTES-PYRENEES (65) 05.05.1999 is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. Its review allowed for a connection to be made with another observation case [AERO LOC] MORTIERS (17) 04.05.1999 (observation from an aircraft), initially deemed unusable (class C). On May 5, 1999, around midnight, nine witnesses located in different towns in the Hautes-Pyrénées department (65) observed a phenomenon in the night sky consisting of a very bright glow followed by a triangular or conical cloud. No unusual noise was heard. During the observations, which varied in duration, the unidentified flying object (UFO) appeared to rotate. The glow disappeared, and the cloud gradually dissipated. This phenomenon was also reported by a pilot (whose aircraft was located south of Cognac). Air traffic control also noted that two other pilots reported seeing the same phenomenon. With very strong evidence (three independent groups of witnesses in the Hautes-Pyrénées, fairly precise information), this case appears to be a highly probable case of mistaken identity involving a missile test launch. Thanks to the internet, access to missile launch records is easier 20 years later than it was at the time of the launches (see the investigation report). The description of the UFO strongly resembles a missile launch, and several witnesses thought it was a rocket launch. While no rocket launch actually corresponds to the observation, it should be noted that two French missile launches took place on May 4, 1999. The UFO sighting, in UTC, does indeed correspond to May 4, 1999. Numerous elements are perfectly consistent with the hypothesis of a misidentification as a missile launch: the directions of observation indicated by the witnesses point towards the Bay of Biscay and the coast of Brittany. Furthermore, the fact that the three geographically distant groups of witnesses saw the UFO under similar conditions shows that it was at a high altitude. Furthermore, the crew of an airliner (case [AERO LOC] MORTIERS (17) 04.05.1999) flying over the Charente region made the same type of observation at the same time. All of this establishes the hypothesis of a misidentification of one of these two missiles, perfectly visible (with distinction between the body and the ejected gases) in the night sky to the witnesses, as the missiles were still in sunlight due to their high altitude. We know that a launch occurred that day and that subsequent launches took place at that precise time. Under these circumstances, the lack of confirmation of the launch time that day is not likely to undermine this hypothesis. It is not reasonable to initiate a procedure (formally cumbersome 20 years later) to contact the test centers to obtain a precise time for the May 4th launch. 1999. . Consequently, GEIPAN combines the two cases of observation into a single case which it classifies as A: very probable observation of a firing of an M45 or M4 defense missile in the Bay of Biscay from off the coast of Brittany.

summary: Observation of two aerial phenomena
description: On March 16, 1999, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness observed the very rapid passage of two aerial phenomena: a small orange sphere and a ball of flames. The trajectory of both spheres was straight, but one of them appeared to plunge into the valley before rising again. The phenomenon remained completely silent and lasted only a few seconds. The trajectory of one of the two phenomena initially ruled out the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry. The proximity of military installations also prevented identification of the phenomenon, which remains unexplained.

summary: Observations of the conjunction of Venus and Jupiter.
description: On February 22nd and 23rd, 1999, at approximately 7:15 PM and 7:30 PM, several witnesses observed one or two stationary points of light in the sky. These points, three or four times larger than a star, intrigued people. The observed phenomenon was the conjunction of the planets Venus and Jupiter, a natural event reported in the media.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On February 5, 1999, two witnesses observed two fireballs falling obliquely from the sky at around 5:30 PM. These were followed by trails of black smoke. The reported observation was probably an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On February 1, 1999, shortly after 7:00 AM, a dozen witnesses in two departments of southeastern France observed a large, luminous sphere with sparks at its rear, which passed by at high speed before disappearing. The phenomenon was silent and lasted only a few seconds. Based on the descriptions given, it was likely an atmospheric reentry.
